links.note: Which crop was growing on Lencho's fields - corn. 24123 names the ripe field of corn whose survival depends on the rain.
Which crop was growing on Lencho's fields - corn, the ripe field the rain was needed for.
What 'the field of corn dotted with flowers' means - the flowers scattered across the ripe corn Lencho welcomed the rain for.
What destroyed Lencho's fields - a hailstorm. 24124 is the hail that leaves the field bare.
The field looked as if it were covered in salt - the state of the field after the hailstones fell.
The field looked as if it were covered in salt - the aftermath of the hail on the crop.
Lencho compared the damage to a plague of locusts - his measure of how completely the hail stripped the field.
How Lencho decided to reach his last resort - through a letter. That letter is 24122.
How much money Lencho asked for - a hundred pesos. 24122 states that sum exactly.
Why the postmaster decided to reply - to preserve Lencho's faith in God. That decision is 24130.
Who read the letter - the postmaster, who then answered it. 24130 is his response.
How he felt when he counted the money - angry. The start of his distrust of the post-office people.
What Lencho thought of the post-office employees - a bunch of crooks. 24133 uses that phrase.
What he asked for in the second letter - the remaining amount, not sent by mail, because he distrusted the staff.
What Lencho's second letter included - a list of further demands, written in distrust of the post office.
What Lencho's letter included - further demands, arising from his belief that the staff had robbed him.
How the house can best be described from its location - solitary. 24120 is the lone house on a low hill.
How the house is best described from its location - solitary, the only one in the whole valley.
Which quote supports the extract - 'Farming is a profession of hope'. The item turns on Lencho being a man of the fields, which is 24126.
The post-office money-order activity: buying the form, paying the clerk, keeping the counterfoil. It works through the very transaction by which the postmaster sent Lencho his money.
What made him angry - counting only seventy pesos and concluding the post-office employees had taken the rest. His distrust of people.
Word puzzle on storm words - cyclone, gale, typhoon, tornado, hurricane, whirlwind - the vocabulary strand that follows the hailstorm that destroyed the crop.
Matching exercise on hope expressions, including wishing for something although it is very unlikely - the unwavering hope 24127 describes in Lencho.
Pre-reading question on having been in great difficulty and feeling only a miracle could help - 24129 is the story's opening question about what to put our faith in.
What kind of conflict the chapter shows - between nature and humans and among humans themselves. The second is the irony of 24132, Lencho accusing his helpers.
Large droplets were equivalent to a ten-cent coin - Lencho's reading of the rain his field needed.
Why Lencho did not try to find out who sent the money - complete faith in God. 24127 is that faith surviving total ruin.
Whether positivity can bring brightness in adverse circumstances - the value question drawn from Lencho's certainty after ruin.
The meaning of 'on the crest of a low hill' - the top of a hill. 24120 is that hill and that house.
Whether the post-office employees were really 'a bunch of crooks' - no, they were the ordinary people who answered his prayer. That is 24131 precisely.
